subject: general
question: Which of the following is the primary reason why copper is widely used as a conductor in electrical wiring?

options.text: Copper has a low melting point.
Copper has high resistance to electricity.
Copper has low resistance and high conductivity.

solution:
The correct answer is __Copper has low resistance and high conductivity**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Copper__ is one of the most widely used materials for electrical wiring.
 
• Copper exhibits low electrical resistance and high conductivity, making it ideal for conducting electricity efficiently.
 
• Its high conductivity ensures minimal energy loss during transmission.
 
• Copper is also durable and resistant to corrosion, which enhances its lifespan in electrical applications.
 
• It can be easily drawn into wires, allowing for flexibility in installation.
 
• While not the most inexpensive metal, its properties provide good value for its cost.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Aluminum as a conductor:**
 
 
• Aluminum is also used as an electrical conductor but has higher resistance compared to copper.
 
• It is lighter and less expensive but requires larger cross-sectional areas to achieve similar conductivity.
 
 
 
• **Silver as a conductor:**
 
 
• Silver has the highest electrical conductivity but is too expensive for most practical applications.
 
• It is used in specialized equipment where cost is not a primary concern.
 
 
 
• **Gold as a conductor:**
 
 
• Gold is an excellent conductor and highly resistant to corrosion.
 
• It is primarily used in high-end electronics where reliability and durability are critical.
